events.title: Indian National Sentenced To Over 19 Years For Plot To Kill US Citizen In New York
events.summary: Nikhil Gupta, an Indian national, was sentenced on 20 November to 235 months in prison for his part in a scheme directed by an Indian government employee to assassinate an attorney and political activist in New York City, the Justice Department said. The target was a Sikh separatist. Canadian and US authorities have linked the plot to a broader effort to target Indian dissidents.

events.title: FBI Investigates Apparent Breach Of National Crime Database
events.summary: The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of the National Crime Information Center, the database that law enforcement agencies across the United States use to share records on wanted and missing people, warrants, stolen property and other criminal justice information. CNN first reported the investigation on 20 November, and the Associated Press and NBC News confirmed it through people familiar with the matter; the FBI declined to comment. It was not immediately clear when the breach occurred, how access was gained or whether data was taken. In September the FBI said it was investigating a hack of its job portal.

events.title: Democrat Mary Peltola Wins Alaska Senate Race
events.summary: Democrat Mary Peltola won Alaska's US Senate race, unseating Republican Senator Dan Sullivan, after the Associated Press called the contest on 17 November. Peltola took just over 50 percent of the vote, avoiding a ranked-choice tabulation. She is the first Democrat to win a Senate race in Alaska since 2008 and will be the first Alaska Native to serve in the US Senate. The result is due to be certified by the state.

events.title: Bomb Found At Ethanol Plant In Peoria Forces Evacuations
events.summary: A bomb was discovered on the afternoon of 13 November at the BioUrja Renewables ethanol plant along the Illinois River in Peoria, Illinois. Residents within a one-mile radius were advised to evacuate. Officials said the device had been rendered safe but described it as a credible threat, and the FBI is investigating. Officials have not said who placed the device or why.

events.title: Tanker Crashes Into Docked Cruise Ship In New Orleans, Injuring More Than 30
events.summary: The tanker Atlantic Asphalt struck the river cruise ship American Heritage while it was docked at the Port of New Orleans on the Mississippi River on 13 November, sending passengers, crew and two police officers into the river. More than 30 people were injured and no one was killed; Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry said all of the nearly 200 people aboard the riverboat were rescued. National Transportation Safety Board officials said a preliminary finding indicates the tanker's steering failed. The port has sued the tanker's owners for at least $1 million in damage.

events.title: Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins Wins Alaska Governor's Race
events.summary: Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, a former state legislator, won the race for governor of Alaska, replacing a Republican administration. At 37, he will be the youngest governor in the state's history. He campaigned on bipartisanship.

events.title: FAA Halts All US Flight Departures In Rare Nationwide Ground Stop
events.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration stopped flights at US airports nationwide on the afternoon of 13 November after a failure in the telecommunications network that links the air traffic control system. The stop lasted several hours and was the first nationwide grounding since January 2023. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin attributed it to a telecommunications outage and said there was no indication of a nefarious act. Cancellations ran into the weekend, and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the system must move off its old telecom network; the administration has asked Congress for $50 billion for air traffic control.

events.title: Cargo Ship Strikes Delaware River Bridge Between Philadelphia And New Jersey
events.summary: The Singapore-flagged cargo ship Strategic Alliance struck the Tacony-Palmyra Bridge over the Delaware River at about 1:15 p.m. on 12 November while the bridge was raised for river traffic, the US Coast Guard said. The damage left the drawbridge unable to close for several hours, causing major traffic backups on the Philadelphia side. No injuries were reported. The bridge reopened that evening with one lane closed, and the cause is under investigation.

events.title: Democrat Cindy Holscher Wins Kansas Governor's Race
events.summary: Democratic state senator Cindy Holscher won the Kansas governor's race, defeating Republican Ty Masterson, the president of the state Senate, according to an Associated Press race call on 12 November. Masterson, who had President Donald Trump's endorsement, conceded and said he had called Holscher to congratulate her. The result keeps the governor's office in Democratic hands when the term-limited Laura Kelly leaves office, in a state that usually votes Republican.

events.title: Democrat Scott Colom Wins Mississippi Senate Race
events.summary: Democrat Scott Colom won Mississippi's US Senate race, defeating Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith after a prolonged count following the 3 November election. Hyde-Smith conceded in a video on 11 November, shortly after the Associated Press called the race: "I respect the decision of Mississippi voters," she said. Mississippi had not elected a Democrat to the Senate in more than 40 years, and Colom will be its first Black senator since Reconstruction.

events.title: US Consumer Prices Rise More Than Expected In October
events.summary: US consumer prices rose a seasonally adjusted 0.4 percent in October, more than expected, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported on 10 November. Core prices, which exclude food and energy, rose 0.3 percent, also more than expected. The bureau did not estimate a yearly inflation rate because last year's government shutdown prevented it from collecting data.

events.title: US Charges Three Alleged Iran-Backed Operatives Over Attacks In Europe And US
events.summary: Federal prosecutors in New York unsealed an eight-count superseding indictment on 10 November charging three men with terrorism-related offences over nearly 20 attacks and attempted attacks in Europe and the United States, which the Justice Department says were carried out in support of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and the Iraqi militia Kata'ib Hizballah. The charges include a September 2026 plot at RAF Fairford in England, where US forces were stationed, and an attempt to bomb a synagogue in New York. One of the men, Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi, has been in US custody since May; the others are Mohsen Mohajeri and Mohammad Ali al-Hassani.

events.title: Idaho Man Sentenced To 18 Years Over ISIS-Inspired Church Attack Plot
events.summary: Alexander Scott Mercurio, 21, of Coeur d'Alene, Idaho, was sentenced in federal court on 10 November to 18 years in prison for attempting to provide material support to the Islamic State group, the Justice Department said. Prosecutors said he had planned to take his father's firearms for a mass-casualty attack on Idaho churches "in the name of ISIS", and also planned to use explosives, knives and a machete. The FBI arrested him on 6 April 2024, one day before the planned attack.

events.title: House Shelves Effort To Impeach Defense Secretary Hegseth
events.summary: The House of Representatives voted 211 to 204 on 10 November to refer articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to the Judiciary Committee, effectively ending the effort. Republican Representative Thomas Massie, who filed the resolution with eight articles of impeachment largely over the war with Iran, was the only Republican to vote with Democrats against the referral.

events.title: Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang Resigns After Foreign Intelligence Inquiry
events.summary: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's chief executive on 12 November, four days after the board opened an independent investigation into reports that he had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. Nvidia named chief financial officer Colette Kress interim chief executive and Harvey Jones chair. Reports linked the inquiry to Huang's relationship with a Singapore-based executive whom a memo circulated among US policymakers described as recruited by China's Ministry of State Security; China denied targeting him. On 16 November President Trump said he backed a campaign to reinstate Huang.

events.title: US Measles Cases Reach Highest Level Since 1991
events.summary: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported 5,182 confirmed measles cases in the United States so far in 2026, the highest annual total since 1991 and more than double the 2,289 cases recorded in 2025. Four people have died of measles this year.

events.title: Catastrophic Flood Hits Tennessee-Georgia State Line
events.summary: Storms caused catastrophic flooding along the Tennessee–Georgia state line on 5 November, described as a 1-in-1,000-year flood event. Swift-water teams rescued dozens of people in the twin towns of McCaysville, Georgia, and Copperhill, Tennessee, and a 56-year-old woman died in floodwaters in Murray County, Georgia. Governor Brian Kemp declared a state of emergency for four counties.

events.title: Twelve Illinois Counties Back Non-Binding Separation Referendums
events.summary: Voters in 12 more Illinois counties approved non-binding referendums on 3 November supporting separation from the state, citing the political influence of Chicago and Cook County, FOX 32 Chicago reported. Voters in 45 counties have now approved such measures since 2020. The votes are advisory; creating a new state would require approval from the Illinois General Assembly and Congress.

events.title: Nine Killed As Business Jet Crashes In Florida
events.summary: A Learjet 60 flying from Austin, Texas, to North Eleuthera in the Bahamas crashed near South Military Trail in Palm Beach County, Florida, near Greenacres, on 1 November, killing all nine people on board. The NTSB said the crew had reported light clear ice and moderate turbulence shortly before the crash.

events.title: Eleven Shot Near Florida A&M Stadium After Homecoming Game
events.summary: Eleven people, including six juveniles, were shot near Bragg Memorial Stadium at Florida A&M University in Tallahassee on the night of 24 October, hours after the school's homecoming football game. Twelve people were injured in all, and police said the shooting followed a physical altercation among people who knew one another. A 15-year-old will be charged as an adult.
